page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r9a.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9T25 processor clocked at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring external cloud block storage for persistent operating system and application data files. Hardware acceleration via discrete GPUs is not present. On the networking interface, the instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps, though it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating configured elastic IPs or NAT gateways for external routing.

From an efficiency standpoint, the 1:8 core-to-memory configuration delivers high memory capacity without incurring the overhead of unneeded compute cores. This profile is suited for memory-intensive workloads such as in-memory caching layers, relational database hosting, real-time analytics engines, and enterprise enterprise-tier application runtimes.

It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs alongside 64.0 GB of memory, delivering a dense 8.0 GB of RAM per core allocation. The instance does not include local physical storage, depending instead on attached remote block storage volumes for persistent data retention. It also operates without integrated GPU hardware accelerators and allocates a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included. By pairing substantial memory capacity with a moderate vCPU footprint, ecs.r9a.2xlarge serves as an efficient compute node for memory-bound workloads, including distributed in-memory caches, operational databases, medium-scale data analytics pipelines, and memory-heavy application backends.
